A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Frame In-N-Out work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–G are readable and can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original Frame In and Frame Out experiments in Tables 2–3, ablations in Appendix D/Table 6, and generated examples and failure cases.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds an original human preference study in Appendix C/Table 6.

M1.justification: The CogVideoX-based architecture, motion and identity conditioning, unbounded canvas, full-field loss and two-stage procedure remain unchanged. Added descriptions of discarding and refreshing text/identity tokens clarify implementation without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenVid-1M, VidGen-1M and a WebVid-10M subset, with the same 183 Frame In and 189 Frame Out evaluation cases and qualitative scenarios. The human study samples existing benchmark videos without expanding task or data coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain DragAnything, Image Conductor, ToRA, Phantom and SkyReels-A2, including the existing motion-description variants. The human study reuses these five named baselines. SkyReals-A2 is corrected to SkyReels-A2, not replaced.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 changes the reported training schedule from 36K iterations per stage to 32K and 50K. Section 6.3 replaces the full-sequence VLM description with 14 evenly sampled frames. Appendix C adds pairwise human evaluation using 30 videos, three raters and 450 comparisons. These reported protocol changes do not establish that the unchanged benchmark tables were rerun.

E4.justification: The inference-resolution, full-field-loss and positional-encoding ablations are retained unchanged, with v1 Table 6 becoming v2 Table 7. Qualitative examples and failure analyses also remain unchanged. The human study adds benchmark preference evaluation rather than a new ablation, robustness test or diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports quantitative uncertainty estimates, repeated-run counts or formal significance tests. Figure 11's qualitative discussion of different random seeds is retained. The new human-study proportions have no uncertainty estimates; its statistical-significance assertion is an interpretation, not a reported test.

E6.justification: New v2 Table 6 reports preference win rates for the proposed method of 83.3% against DragAnything, 100.0% against Image Conductor, 73.3% against ToRA, 91.1% against Phantom and 92.2% against SkyReels-A2. All numerical entries in Tables 2–3 and the matched ablation table remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, architecture and loss equations, metric formulas and appendix camera-motion score are unchanged. No new assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the Frame In/Out task, curated data, unified conditioning architecture and evaluation demonstrating advantages over existing baselines. Contribution wording changes and added supporting evidence do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly interprets human preferences as corroborating automatic metrics and claims that consistency supports statistical significance, without reporting a formal test. Existing explanations and limitations concerning pose, object size, camera motion and canvas color distortion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds token-handling details, CoTracker-based SAM2 prompting, exact VLM instructions and response handling, and a promise to release preprocessing code alongside metadata. Conversely, it removes the stated 8-bit Adam optimizer and the 20%/33% speed-up augmentation probabilities. These omissions do not establish an optimizer or augmentation change.

R1.justification: v2 adds FlexiAct to the video-to-video related-work citations and removes the 8-bit optimizers reference alongside the optimizer disclosure. The broader positioning relative to motion control, identity conditioning and video outpainting remains intact.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the abstract, contributions and flexible-resolution explanation, grammar and terminology corrections, and updated conference and acknowledgment text. Appendix C gains a human-study subsection, while the overall section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the human-study table, relocates Table 2 and renumbers the retained ablation table. Tables 1 and 5 gain colored checks and crosses, several captions are refined, and pages reflow. The illustrated content of Figures 1–11 is retained.

improvement.justification: The human preference study adds direct subjective support beyond v1's automatic metrics and qualitative examples, while the added token-handling and VLM details improve clarity. These are modest gains: optimizer and augmentation disclosures are lost, revised settings are not linked to rerun results, and the new statistical-significance interpretation exceeds the reported analysis.
